tier_reason: doc/markdown/benchmarks.md compares doctest 2.2.0 against Catch 2.3.0 using the public harness scripts/bench/bench.py (generates the sources and CMakeLists, downloads catch.hpp 2.3.0, times cmake --build) driven by scripts/bench/run_all.py, with compiler versions and the CPU (Intel i7 3770k) stated; flags are fixed by the script (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Debug/Release, -std=c++11, -w), so the setup is reproducible.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: MSVC 2017 15.8.1, MinGW-w64 GCC 8.1.0, Linux GCC 6.3.0, Linux Clang 4.0.0. scripts/bench/bench.py configures CMake with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Debug or Release (so CMake's default per-config flags apply: -O3 -DNDEBUG for GCC/Clang Release, /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG for MSVC Release), adds -std=c++11 on non-MSVC and -w on GCC/Clang, and builds single-threaded with cmake --build; scripts/bench/run_all.py averages 3 runs per table cell.
corrections.caveats: The project's own benchmark (Dec 2018): doctest 2.2.0 against Catch 2.3.0, both far behind current releases; Catch2 v3 became a compiled library with a different compile-time profile and was not measured. Flags come from the public script (CMake build-type defaults) rather than the page text. Linux numbers come from a VirtualBox VM on a HDD. run_all.py at HEAD averages 3 runs per cell, but the page gives no variance, and bench.py has been edited since the 2018 run (a 2019 fix, a 2025 newline/encoding chore, a 2026 cmake_minimum_required bump to 3.14), so a rerun uses a slightly different script. Runtime for plain asserts is near parity on GCC and Clang Release (0.29s vs 0.29s, 0.28s vs 0.32s); the large runtime win is only with INFO logging (the page's 'over 18 times faster' case is MSVC Debug, 11.41s vs 213.91s). README says compile time is better 'by orders of magnitude', while the tables show roughly 9-10x on whole-build header cost and up to about 8x on assert macros (MSVC Release 58.73s vs 448.68s; Linux GCC Release only about 2.4x, derived from page data). Google Test and Boost.Test are not benchmarked on the page. doctest is a unit-testing framework whose speed claim is compile time; it does not cache or distribute builds.

notes: All claimed_speedup numbers match the page rows.
